<!--
  Forge Release Notes Template
  ============================
  Every Forge release uses this template. The release engineer copies it
  to docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md, fills it in, and commits it in the same
  PR as the release tag. The release pipeline attaches the file to the
  GitHub release.

  Rules:
    1. Every heading is required unless explicitly marked optional.
    2. The "Breaking changes" section is required for MAJOR bumps and
       for any v0.x.0 bump that breaks compatibility. It may be omitted
       only when the release has no breaking changes.
    3. The "Security" section is required when the release contains a
       security fix. Omit it otherwise. Do not describe a vulnerability
       in detail until users have had time to upgrade; link to a
       GitHub Security Advisory for the full text.
    4. The "Full changelog" line is generated by the pipeline. Do not
       edit it by hand.
    5. Artifact SHA-256 values are filled in by the pipeline. Do not
       invent them.
    6. Delete these comments before committing.

  Normative references:
    - Versioning scheme: docs/reference/versioning.md
    - Release channels:  docs/reference/release-channels.md
    - ADR:               docs/decisions/ADR-043-versioning-and-release-channels.md

  A release that violates any of rules 1-3 fails the release pipeline's
  notes check.
-->

# Forge vX.Y.Z

**Channel:** stable | prerelease | nightly
**Released:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Commit:** `<short-sha>`
**Build type:** release | ci | local

## Summary

One paragraph. What does this release do, and who should care? Written
for a user who has not been following the issue tracker. Avoid jargon.
If the release is a patch, say what was broken and what is fixed. If the
release adds a feature, say what the feature does and how to use it in
one sentence. Do not list every commit; that is the changelog's job.

## Breaking changes

<!--
  Required for MAJOR bumps and for v0.x.0 bumps that break compatibility.
  Omit the entire section if there are no breaking changes.

  Each entry names the surface (CLI, forge.yaml, exit codes, output
  format) and tells the user what to do. Link to a migration guide if
  one exists.

  For a MAJOR bump, this section is the most important part of the
  release. Do not bury it below "Added".

  For a v0.x.0 bump, this section is required only if a change is
  actually breaking. A v0.x.0 release that adds only features omits it.
-->

- **<surface>**: <what changed and what the user must do>.
  See [migration guide](../guides/migrating-to-vX.md).
- **<surface>**: <what changed and what the user must do>.

## Added

<!--
  New commands, flags, fields, formats, platforms. Omit if none.
  Each entry links to the relevant documentation page. Keep entries to
  one sentence; the linked page has the detail.
-->

- <new command or flag>. See [docs](../reference/cli.md#new-thing).
- <new forge.yaml field>. See [forge.yaml spec](../reference/forge-yaml-spec.md).

## Changed

<!--
  Behaviour changes that are not breaking. Omit if none.
  "Changed" is for observable differences that a user might notice but
  that do not require action. If the change requires action, it belongs
  in "Breaking changes".
-->

- <behaviour change>. <one-line rationale>.
- <behaviour change>. <one-line rationale>.

## Fixed

<!--
  Bug fixes. Omit if none. Each entry names the symptom, not the
  internal cause. Link to the issue if there is one.

  Example:
    - `forge check` no longer reports a false positive on symlinked
      directories. Closes #123.
-->

- <bug fix>. Closes #<issue>.
- <bug fix>. Closes #<issue>.

## Security

<!--
  Required when the release contains a security fix. Omit otherwise.

  Do not describe the vulnerability in detail here. Link to a GitHub
  Security Advisory for the full text. Users who read release notes may
  not have upgraded yet; a detailed description gives attackers a head
  start.
-->

- **<GHSA-id or CVE-id>**: <one-line summary>. Upgrade recommended.
  See the [advisory](https://github.com/thapelomagqazana/forge/security/advisories/<id>)
  for details.

## Deprecated

<!--
  Features, flags, or fields that are deprecated but still work. Omit
  if none. Each entry names the replacement and the target removal
  version.
-->

- <surface>: deprecated in favour of <replacement>. Removal planned
  for v<next-major>.0.0.

## Upgrade notes

<!--
  Manual steps a user must take beyond swapping the binary. Omit if
  upgrade is a simple binary swap.

  Example:
    - If you use `forge.yaml` with a `logLevel` field, rename it to
      `log.level` before upgrading. The old field is accepted with a
      deprecation warning in v1.x and will be rejected in v2.0.0.
-->

## Distribution

<!--
  Filled in by the pipeline from docs/reference/platforms.yaml and
  docs/reference/version-metadata.yaml. For a prerelease or nightly
  release, only the channels that channel supports are listed.

  Do not edit this table by hand.
-->

| Channel | Command |
|---|---|
| Direct | <https://forge.dev/download/vX.Y.Z> |
| Homebrew | `brew upgrade forge` (stable only) |
| Scoop | `scoop update forge` (stable only) |
| winget | `winget upgrade Forge.Forge` (stable only) |
| apt | `apt-get install --only-upgrade forge` (stable only) |
| Docker | `docker pull ghcr.io/forge/forge:vX.Y.Z` |

  Filled in by the pipeline. Do not edit by hand.
  SHA-256 values come from the signed release manifest.
-->

| linux/arm64 | `forge-vX.Y.Z-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `<sha256>` |
| darwin/amd64 | `forge-vX.Y.Z-darwin-amd64.tar.gz` | `<sha256>` |
| darwin/arm64 | `forge-vX.Y.Z-darwin-arm64.tar.gz` | `<sha256>` |

| windows/arm64 | `forge-vX.Y.Z-windows-arm64.zip` | `<sha256>` |

Verify the release signature:

```sh
cosign verify-blob \
  --certificate forge-vX.Y.Z-linux-amd64.tar.gz.pem \
  --signature   forge-vX.Y.Z-linux-amd64.tar.gz.sig \
  forge-vX.Y.Z-linux-amd64.tar.gz
```
